outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Memory and lithography-adjacent chips, led by Micron, ASML, and Synopsys
strongest.reason: all three extended sharp rebounds today even as the broader AI-chip trade stayed choppy, continuing to unwind the multi-week selloff that hit memory and equipment names

strongest.area: AI infrastructure buildout, driven by fresh capex commitments
strongest.reason: Anthropic's newly announced $50 billion U.S. data-center investment and a new Google-Blackstone joint venture for TPU-powered data centers underscore continued infrastructure spending momentum, even though individual megacap and chip-adjacent stocks were mixed to lower today

weakest.area: Enterprise AI software, led by Adobe, Salesforce, Palantir, and ServiceNow
weakest.reason: all four fell 2-3% again today, extending a months-long selloff pattern where even solid earnings have been met with selling on fears that AI agents could erode subscription pricing power

weakest.area: Cybersecurity, led by CrowdStrike and Zscaler
weakest.reason: both pulled back today after last week's Black Hat-driven record highs, likely some profit-taking following a strong multi-week run even as the underlying AI-threat demand narrative stays intact

outlook.nextStep: The enterprise software selloff is worth a closer look for whether it's starting to separate fundamentals from AI-disruption sentiment, especially after Nvidia's CEO recently pushed back publicly on the bearish narrative. The sharp swings in chip names (Broadcom down sharply today while Micron and ASML surged) are probably better watched for confirmation over the next few sessions than acted on now, given how volatile the sector has been.

signals.title: July CPI came in cool, easing pressure on the Fed ahead of September
signals.body: July CPI rose just 0.1% month-over-month, with headline inflation at 3.4% year-on-year and core at 2.5%, both down a tenth of a point from June. The Fed held rates steady at its July meeting in a 9-3 vote, keeping the target range at 3.5%-3.75%, and the tame reading has reduced near-term urgency for further action ahead of the September meeting.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether the next inflation print confirms this cooling trend, since that's what markets are now pricing in for a September hold

signals.title: AI chip trade stays volatile after weeks of profit-taking
signals.body: Chip stocks have swung sharply in recent weeks after a period of heavy profit-taking unwound some of the AI-driven run-up; memory names in particular were hit hard before rebounding. Today's action was similarly split, with Micron, ASML, and Synopsys all posting strong gains while Broadcom fell nearly 6%.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether the sector is stabilizing or still working through a broader repricing, given how wide the swings between individual names have been

signals.title: Anthropic and Google deepen AI infrastructure buildout commitments
signals.body: Anthropic announced a $50 billion investment in U.S. computing infrastructure, building data centers with Fluidstack in Texas and New York with more sites planned. Separately, Google and Blackstone formed a joint venture to build TPU-powered data centers to meet growing AI compute demand. Industry forecasts project the AI infrastructure market to grow from roughly $76 billion in 2026 to over $220 billion by 2030.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at which infrastructure suppliers and cloud providers are best positioned to capture this spending, independent of today's mixed price action

signals.title: Enterprise software selloff continues despite pushback from Nvidia's CEO
signals.body: Adobe, Salesforce, Palantir, and ServiceNow all fell 2-3% again today, extending a pattern seen through the year where even companies beating earnings estimates have sold off on fears that AI agents will disrupt per-seat subscription pricing. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang recently pushed back on the bearish narrative, calling it 'an incredible time to be a software company,' which sparked a brief relief rally in prior sessions that has since faded.
signals.focus: lower conviction right now given how persistent the selling pressure has been despite periodic optimistic commentary

signals.title: Cybersecurity pulls back after Black Hat-driven record highs
signals.body: CrowdStrike and Zscaler both eased today after surging to record highs last week following the Black Hat conference, where analysts highlighted how AI agents have changed the threat landscape and are driving fresh security-budget spending. Today's move looks like profit-taking after a strong multi-week run rather than a shift in the underlying demand story.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether this is a routine pullback or the start of a broader cooling, given how sharply the group had run up

signals.title: Crypto regulatory path grows more uncertain
signals.body: Galaxy Digital cut its estimated odds of the CLARITY Act passing in 2026 to just 10%, citing unresolved political issues and a narrow two-to-three-week Senate window after it reconvenes on September 14. The SEC also abruptly postponed a planned vote on new crypto capital-raising rules, and Binance is set to cut off access to several trading platforms, including HTX, starting August 23 over sanctions-related compliance concerns.
signals.focus: lower conviction on near-term regulatory catalysts given both the legislative and SEC timelines just slipped further

signals.title: Humanoid robotics remains a mostly private, pre-revenue story
signals.body: Public market exposure to humanoid robotics is still concentrated in component suppliers and established industrial or surgical robotics names, since most of the leading humanoid robotics developers remain private. Industry forecasts put the current humanoid market at just $2-3 billion today, with projections ranging widely up to $200 billion by 2035, underscoring how early and speculative the space still is.
signals.focus: worth treating public-market robotics exposure as an indirect and early-stage bet rather than a direct read on humanoid adoption timelines
